sources.note: Nothing; no phonology section at all. Corpus described as c. 120 words (names and glosses in Greek/Latin transcription). Bibliography: Eska 2006 (Koch encyclopedia III: 788), Eska 2013 (ZcP 60: 51-64), Freeman 2001, Delamarre 2003, Weisgerber 1931.

sources.citation: Colvin, Stephen. 2002. Review of Philip Freeman, The Galatian Language: A Comprehensive Survey of the Language of the Ancient Celts in Greco-Roman Asia Minor (Lewiston: Mellen, 2001). Bryn Mawr Classical Review 2002.12.19.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Review characterises Freeman 2001 as a chrestomathy of classical passages plus four lists of names (personal, tribal, divine, place) in nine unnumbered sections; 'nothing survives except personal names'; no phonology or accent discussion is mentioned anywhere in the review.

sources.note: Nothing; classification/status page only. Refs listed: Weisgerber 1931; Freeman 2001; Eska 2017: 1270-71; Eska & Evans 2010: 42. Only descriptive ref in the bibliography (De Hoz 1997, ZcP 49-50) is on verbal -i, not stress.
